learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the fun of printmaking by turning simple objects into stamps to create repeating patterns and designs!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Thousands of years ago, people used special carved stones called seals to stamp their mark on clay. This was the very first step toward learning how to print!
Printmaking is an awesome technique where you create an image once on a surface, cover it in ink or paint, and press it onto paper. You can copy the exact same image over and over again!
When you stamp the same shape multiple times in a row or in a circle, you create a pattern. Patterns look beautiful on wrapping paper, fabrics, and wall borders.
You don't need fancy tools to print! You can dip leaves, cut vegetables, or even your own fingertips in paint to stamp amazing natural shapes onto your page.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 Veggie Print Party
fun_activity.instructions: Ask an adult to cut a ladyfinger or a potato in half. Dip the cut side into water colors or poster paints and press it onto a blank paper to make your own colorful, repeating border pattern!

quick_recap: ⭐ Seals were some of the earliest tools people used to stamp marks on clay.
⭐ Printmaking lets you create one design and print it many times without redrawing it.
⭐ Stamping shapes in an organized way helps you build beautiful, repeating patterns.
⭐ Everyday items like leaves, erasers, and vegetables make excellent DIY printing stamps.
